title: Alleged mastermind behind Rs. 21 Billion illegal Dollar transfer network arrested
summary: The Financial Investigation Division has arrested the alleged mastermind behind a large-scale money laundering operation accused of illegally transferring more than Rs. 21 billion (over US$700 million) out of Sri Lanka under the guise of importing goods.

title: Police sound alarm over social media romance scams
summary: The Sri Lanka Police has issued a public advisory warning citizens, particularly women, to remain vigilant against romance scams and other forms of fraud carried out through social media and digital communication platforms.

title: IMF team to visit Sri Lanka next week to review reform programme
summary: A team from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) will visit Sri Lanka from June 24 to June 30 for a staff mission aimed at reviewing recent economic developments and the country’s ongoing reform programme.

title: Iran negotiators, Vance head for Switzerland but Lebanon fighting continues
summary: A high-level Iranian team arrived in Switzerland on Saturday for peace talks with the U.S., Iranian state media reported, as U.S. Vice President JD Vance departed Washington for meetings that Pakistan said will begin on Sunday.

title: Which teams have qualified for the FIFA World Cup 2026 knockouts, round of 32?

title: Fuel price relief possible by August or September if global prices remain stable: Bimal
summary: The government could pass on the benefits of lower global fuel prices to the public by August or September, provided international fuel prices remain at their current levels, Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development Bimal Rathnayake said.

title: Three-month concession given for vehicles without seatbelts
summary: The National Council for Road Safety said that a final three-month grace period will be given for owners of vehicles that were originally manufactured without seatbelts to install the required safety equipment.

title: Pakistan cuts petrol price by Rs74 after US-Iran peace deal eases oil costs
summary: Pakistan on Friday slashed fuel prices by up to Rs74 per liter after a peace agreement between the United States and Iran helped ease pressure on global oil markets, with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif saying the government was passing on the full benefit of lower international prices to consumers.

title: Iran closes Strait of Hormuz over ceasefire violations - MEHR
summary: Iran’s top joint military command, Khatam al-Anbiya Central ‌Headquarters, said on Saturday that the Strait of Hormuz would be closed to vessel ⁠traffic, citing alleged violations of a ceasefire agreement by the U.S. and Israel, Iran’s Mehr state news agency reported.

title: Final weekend to see Dehiwala Zoo’s lion cubs up close
summary: The special opportunity for visitors to see the two lion cubs born at the Dehiwala Zoological Gardens from close range will end on Sunday (June 21), with the Department of National Zoological Gardens urging the public to make the most of the final weekend.

title: At least seven killed in twin roadside bombings in northwest Pakistan
summary: Two roadside bombs in restive northwestern Pakistan killed at least seven people on Saturday, authorities said.

title: Seat belt law comes into force across Sri Lanka from today
summary: The National Council for Road Safety announced that the mandatory enforcement of Sri Lanka’s seat belt law comes into effect from today (20), following the conclusion of the grace period granted for motorists.

title: Australia vows to rein in any H5N1 birdflu after confirming first case
summary: Australia will do all it can to curb any spread of H5N1 bird flu, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Saturday, as the first mainland infection was confirmed ‌in a seabird a day after being detected in a remote southwestern region.
